$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{{field-1}}=-{X}_{1}(s) \\ {{field-2}}={{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-3L{{x}_{1}(t)}-4L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2=-{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-7=-3{X}_{1}(s)-4{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{3{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=3L{{x}_{1}(t)}+4L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2=2{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=3{X}_{1}(s)+4{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)-2=2{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2}{s-2}.
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)+1=3(\frac{2}{s-2})+4{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-s+8}{(s-2)(s-4)}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}-2L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+2L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-9={X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-6=-{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}(s-1){X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)=9 \\ {X}_{1}(s)+(s-2){X}_{2}(s)=6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s).
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-1)[6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s)]+2{X}_{2}(s) & =9 \\ 6(s-1)-[(s-1)(s-2)-2]{X}_{2}(s) & =9 \\ -({s}^{2}-3s){X}_{2}(s) & =9-6(s-1) \\ -s(s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =-6s+15 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s) \\  & =6-(s-2)\cdot \frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{6s(s-3)-3(s-2)(2s-5)}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{3(3s-10)}{s(s-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3(3s-10)}{s(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}=\frac{1}{s}+\frac{1}{s-2},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s-2}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{2t}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}+\frac{1}{s-2}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}} \\  & =1+{e}^{2\cdot t} \\  & =1+{e}^{2t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s-2}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}} \\  & =1-{e}^{2\cdot t} \\  & =1-{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+{e}^{2t} \\ 1-{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}=\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}=\frac{4}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{6t}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1+{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4+{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1-{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}=\frac{1}{s}+\frac{4}{s-6},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}=\frac{5}{s}-\frac{4}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{6t}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}+\frac{4}{s-6}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =1+4{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =1+4{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{5}{s}-\frac{4}{s-6}} \\  & =5{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =5-4{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =5-4{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+4{e}^{6t} \\ 5-4{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14074064/assets/075eca4fcc837dce57c4bcfba01047af3d72f15b80cd3fabfc7e5b00be83813d.png)
Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $\mathcal{L}$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables $X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\!\left\{  x_1(t) \right\}$ and $X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\!\left\{  x_2(t) \right\}.$ 
Find the solution of the new system in terms of the parameter $s.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L\,{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L\,{-3{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L\,{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L\,{3{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL\,{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=-3L\,{{x}_{1}(t)}+L\,{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL\,{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=3L\,{{x}_{1}(t)}-L\,{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-4=-3{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-4=3{X}_{1}(s)-{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where $X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\!\left\{  x_1(t) \right\}$ and $X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\!\left\{  x_2(t) \right\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}(s+3){X}_{1}(s)-{X}_{2}(s)=4 \\ -3{X}_{1}(s)+(s+1){X}_{2}(s)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the first equation, we have

$$
X_2(s) = (s+3)X_1(s) - 4.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{X}_{1}(s)+(s+1)\,[(s+3){X}_{1}(s)-4] & =4 \\ -3{X}_{1}(s)+(s+1)(s+3){X}_{1}(s)-4(s+1) & =4 \\ [(s+1)(s+3)-3]{X}_{1}(s) & =4+4(s+1) \\ s(s+4){X}_{1}(s) & =4s+8 \\ {X}_{1}(s)=\frac{4(s+2)}{s(s+4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $X_2(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{2}(s) & =(s+3){X}_{1}(s)-4 \\  & =(s+3)\,(\frac{4(s+2)}{s(s+4)})-4 \\  & =\frac{4(s+3)(s+2)-4s(s+4)}{s(s+4)} \\  & =\frac{4({s}^{2}+5s+6)-4({s}^{2}+4s)}{s(s+4)} \\  & =\frac{4{s}^{2}+20s+24-4{s}^{2}-16s}{s(s+4)} \\  & =\frac{4(s+6)}{s(s+4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
X_1(s) =\dfrac{4(s+2)}{s(s+4)}, 
\qquad
X_2(s) = \dfrac{4(s+6)}{s(s+4)}.
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_1(t) \right\} = \dfrac{4}{s} + \dfrac{1}{s-6}, 
\qquad
X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_2(t) \right\} = \dfrac{20}{s} - \dfrac{1}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to $X_1(s)$ and $X_2(s){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1+{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4+{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{20}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =20{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =20\cdot 1-{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+{e}^{6t} \\ 20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 20\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$
